Proposes a responsible AI integration framework for psychiatric clinical guidelines. Addresses clinical AI deployment ethics, not computational tools for literature discovery, screening, or synthesis. Falls under EXC-02 (non-scholarly domain - clinical practice framework).

Narrative review of generative AI applications in ophthalmology education. Discusses LLM capabilities/challenges but does not propose, implement, or evaluate a computational harness for literature review workflows. Falls under EXC-03 (narrative piece lacking computational artifact for evidence synthesis).

Editorial arguing for behavioral safety testing of AI companion chatbots. Opinion piece on regulation/clinical safety, not a computational tool for literature review or evidence synthesis. Falls under EXC-03 (narrative commentary lacking computational artifact).

Title indicates comparison of dental knowledge across LLMs. No abstract available, but scope appears to be domain-specific knowledge evaluation, not a literature review harness or evidence synthesis tool. Falls under EXC-02 (general LLM evaluation not targeted to scholarly literature workflow).

Proposes and validates a locally executed multi-agent AI framework for deduplication, screening, and structured data extraction in systematic reviews (spine surgery). Explicitly incorporates LLMs/agentic orchestration (INC-02), describes execution provenance via PRISMA-trAIce compliance and local execution for data governance (INC-03), and provides quantitative empirical evaluation across 3 SRs with Cohen's κ, accuracy, time savings, and critical error rates (INC-04). Directly addresses all three RQs: architecture/provenance (RQ1), trust/integrity mechanisms including hallucination checks (RQ2), and empirical evaluation with benchmarks (RQ3).

Plant metabolomics review on environmental stress responses. No connection to AI research harnesses, literature review automation, or evidence synthesis tools. Falls under EXC-02 (non-scholarly domain - plant biology).

Empirical study critically assessing ChatGPT (GPT-4) for data extraction in systematic reviews (COVID-19 modeling studies). Evaluates LLM performance on explicit vs. contextual data extraction with iterative prompt refinement, reporting accuracy metrics (71.7% final accuracy, 93.3% for explicit settings). Matches INC-01 (evaluates computational tool for evidence synthesis), INC-02 (uses LLMs in literature workflow), INC-04 (quantitative empirical evaluation with benchmarks). Addresses RQ1 (LLM-based extraction architecture), RQ2 (hallucination/accuracy limitations), RQ3 (empirical evaluation with iterative prompting).

Policy framework for agentic generative AI in cancer care (SSRN preprint). No abstract available, but title indicates clinical policy/architecture focus, not a computational harness for literature review or evidence synthesis. Falls under EXC-03 (policy manifesto lacking computational artifact for scholarly workflow).
Published in 2020, predating the 2023–2026 LLM era. Discusses AI impact on radiography profession, not literature review harnesses. Falls under EXC-04 (temporal out of bounds).

Introduces ENTGPT (GPT-4o based) with novel STARR protocol for systematic review screening in otolaryngology. Evaluates LLM against human reviewers with traditional vs. STARR protocols, reporting accuracy (99.87%), sensitivity (95%), specificity (100%), and CI. Matches INC-01 (computational tool for literature screening), INC-02 (LLM/agentic orchestration), INC-04 (quantitative empirical evaluation with benchmarks). Addresses RQ1 (screening architecture/protocol), RQ2 (accuracy/hallucination mitigation via STARR re-evaluation), RQ3 (empirical evaluation with inter-rater comparison).

Comment/letter on bariatric surgery complications study. No computational tool, literature workflow, or evidence synthesis system described. Falls under EXC-03 (narrative commentary lacking computational artifact).
